get_api.description: Look one API up by its provider, and the service name when it has one, and get back everything the directory knows about it: the title, the full description, the categories and tags, the logo, the licence and terms of service, whom to contact and where to register an app for credentials, when it was added and last updated, every version it holds and the one it recommends, and the addresses of its OpenAPI definition in JSON and YAML - ready to fetch with an HTTP step or hand to a code generator. Name a version to describe that one instead of the recommended one. No account or API key required.

get_metrics.description: Read the directory's own numbers: how many APIs, providers, definitions and endpoints it holds, how many definitions are unofficial, unreachable or invalid, and how many APIs were added and updated in the week before the directory was last rebuilt, with the date the figures were last published. The directory is rebuilt now and then rather than every day, and its weekly counts can be years older than that date. The figures the project puts on its front page, for a dashboard. No account or API key required.

list_api_endpoints.description: List the endpoints one API offers - each one's method, path and what it does - read from the OpenAPI definition the directory holds for it, with the addresses the API is served from and how a caller signs in: OAuth, an API key and where it goes, or a bearer token. Look the API up by provider, and service when it has one; the version is the recommended one unless you name another. Filter by a word or by method, and page through with a limit and an offset: GitHub's API has over 800 endpoints and Amazon EC2's over 1,100. The way to find which call does what you need before building an HTTP step. Definitions larger than 16 MB, such as Microsoft Graph's, are refused, and the step says where to fetch them instead. No account or API key required.

description: The Wikipedia for Web APIs: a free, open directory of machine-readable API definitions in OpenAPI format, covering thousands of APIs from hundreds of providers - Google, Microsoft, Amazon, GitHub, Twilio and many more. Search it by keyword or category, list a provider's APIs and services, look one API up by name and version to get its title, description, licence, logo and the address of its OpenAPI definition in JSON or YAML, list the endpoints its definition describes and how to sign in to it, or read the directory's own metrics. For workflows that discover APIs, catalogue them or feed their definitions into other tools. API definitions supplied by APIs.guru (https://apis.guru). No account or API key required.
